lines.text: The grain is no longer being held against a signature. Keeping it moving will take more than words.
Hunger does not make an oath freely given.
They have not taken it down. Somebody is afraid enough to cover it and kind enough to keep it dry.
A private account can still invite a second witness.
Keeping the token is not the same as keeping them safe.
Mind the cup on the step. The man from the south road needs it more than I need a clean floor.
I read the road notice. Three missing.
Bram drove. Sella had Oren beside her. He left his coat here because the sun was out.
They found old wooden tokens where the road was being repaired. Sella asked me to read one. I did.
What happened when you read it?
The candles went out. I sent them away while I found a rite I thought would keep them safe.
If you find red thread around black feathers, keep it intact. I tied it. I owe you that much before you go.
Thank you for the water. Now, the three who have not come home.
I have put the grain list beside the burial book. No one has to sign one to receive the other.
I could call that a beginning. It is mostly a table and two people willing to sit at it.
Beginnings usually look smaller when somebody is doing the work.
I will give you the register. I am not agreeing to stand in a rite you threatened me into.
The record can speak to facts. It cannot make your promise for you.
Then you do understand the difference.
Edric wants my hand on the new seal. He has already counted the households that cannot afford to refuse.
The old rite borrowed consent from frightened people. That is why it keeps breaking.
Can the Hart be released without making everyone here swear?
Yes. Someone must freely keep the recovered account. One person can begin. More people can share the work.
Three strokes. A burial, a restored name, and a promise that has stopped holding.
I cut the rope last winter. A novice heard an erased name and walked into the sealed chapel. I found him too late.
You closed it again.
Yes. I told myself I was buying time. The graves will show what that time cost.
That is Oren's carving. Turn it over. The older name is beneath his paint.
You sent them out carrying something the shrine had erased.
I thought new burial thread would quiet it. Someone bound it again with Vargan wire.
The pack is dead. The people hiding this are alive.
Take your payment if you must. I need help I have no right to order.
I saw the token on the board. Rook has moved his bedding from the window.
People needed to know what was on their road.
Yes. And the people who can explain it need a way to survive being known.
Then we do both. I will not leave the second part to a notice.
Keep your hand closed if you need to. I recognize the shape through your glove.
Oren painted over a refugee's token. Sella wanted the first name restored.
Someone alive tried to take it from the pack.
Then leaving now would leave a witness carrying something dangerous. I am asking you to stay.
Toma's daughter has a fever. The draught works. The roots it needs grow in the old ash beds.
Does Toma know where it comes from?
He knows I can bring the fever down. I have let him think that was the only fact that mattered.
Sella bought salve for Oren's hands. Too much carving. I have one jar she never collected.
You did not make the fever disappear by closing the ash bed.
No. Who needs help while the new treatment catches up?
Toma. He has not slept. Bring him the broth before it cools.
I treated all five. Consent would mean little if refusal meant I stopped caring.
What will you say at the assembly?
What I used. What I withheld. What I am changing.
There is your immediate result. A child is breathing easier.
And the part he still cannot choose?
Still here. Under the label I have not written.
It is a memory, not a patient who can answer me. I will not call a useful response permission.
Study what is already exposed. Do not open another name without asking the family.
The oil shows where the memory is caught. It does not decide what you should do with it.
And breaking the vessel?
Stops that shape. The memory goes somewhere else. We can defend ourselves without pretending the aftermath is nothing.
Oren restored a name on his token. The road's concealment could not keep it disordered afterward.
That brought the creatures?
The tokens drew them. The failed binding left the memory loose. Read the register before you face what took it.
Your seal was wrapped around a child's token.
My men were sent to contain a breach. They came back with empty hands and fewer men.
I have grain for Greyfen. I do not have a road that will carry it safely.
And the people who know why?
Bring their account to the castle. I will show you what another winter requires.
My guards can keep a road open. They cannot make the people on it believe me.
Begin with the first job. The second takes longer.
I have watched people be told safety was inside a gate they could not enter.
Then come to the record hall. Argue where the figures are.
You got the cart moving? Good. I was about to sell him a very expensive push.
Bram fixed my axle twice. Charged me once. Claimed he could not afford to be seen with a grateful smuggler.
You knew the other two?
Sella asked about the old road. Oren asked whether the crows paid me to follow them.
The road bends where the old waystone says it should not. I have a map. I also have a room somebody can find.
They copied the map with my family mark still on it. A guard came to my door.
You needed a witness. You got a target as well.
I will keep a way out open.
That was meant to be the promise before you put my name up.
I copied the route without the houses. The families know who has the original.
I will tell the assembly what I saw. They do not need my grandmother's bedroom to believe it.
You choose what is yours to share.
There. A sentence I could get used to.
I can still walk the route. I will not make another map for you.
Destroying the copy kept Vargan from using it. It kept the next refugee from using it too.
I can carry the route in the record without your family mark.
Then learn it properly.
The guard asked where my grandmother lived. Said he was checking who deserved protection.
My family kept names because the shrine would not. That does not make us willing to be nailed to a board.
I promised to stay with the people carrying this.
Then stay where they can reach you. The false waystone is a good start.
You can know that and still hear what I ask next.
His grave bell rings with the rope cut. He helped close Greyfen's gate in the war. I told our children he held it for their safety.
Did he ever speak about the people outside?
He would stop setting the table when it rained. Find what he left. Do not decide for me that love makes me unable to hear it.
My daughter asked if both were true. I said yes.
Will you speak at the assembly?
About what I know. His victims do not need me performing my grief over their names.
You offered me a gentler account. I heard what you left out.
The record remains.
Then leave it where the children can find it when they ask.
You may name what Harl did. You may not use my kitchen as proof I have forgiven it.
Your grief stays yours.
The forge still runs. If the road goes, every household will want a latch before they want a sword.
There are letters ground off this iron.
Refugee marks. I recognized them years ago. Told myself metal did not care who used it next.
Some of it is holding doors shut against the rain. You want it back, tell me what we put in its place.
I am replacing one working piece at a time. Elna still has a door while I make the marker.
What did it cost?
Two contracts. A late night. Less than grinding those letters off cost somebody else.
The tools stay useful. A share of each sale goes to replacement iron and the road record.
You will say that publicly?
I already wrote it above the price.
Anwen will keep it until the families decide. I work from new scrap now.
Is the forge closing?
Not if you stop talking and help carry the clean iron.
My daughter was outside when the bandits came. The thing at the fold put itself between her and a blade.
And the missing sheep?
I fed it. Then I hid it. It started taking from the next field and I kept telling myself gratitude was different from a danger.
Read the boot marks with the tracks. I want the whole cause found, even the part that is mine.
The creature follows the old protection path beyond the fields. I warned the neighbors this time.
A boundary only works if everyone knows where it is.
I do not call it harmless. I call the neighbors before I feed it.
They get to change their minds.
Yes. Even when I wish they would not.
I told her about the sheep. And that I hid it until there were no easy choices left.
Keep its protection in the account too.
I heard it at the next field last night. I will not tell you I was surprised.
Hold the gate. Hold the gate. The lantern is on the wrong side.
You are repeating one night. Can you tell me your name?
Len. Mother left the lantern. Hold the gate.
A fragment caught in an empty grave. Not a man who knows what happened afterward.
Len. The lantern is on the wrong side.
You have kept the account where a living hand can reach it. That is something the old oath would not allow.
The grain condition is broken. No one standing here has to promise you anything to eat.
I remember the gate shut. I remember the road hidden. I remember the soldiers entering. I will not tell you those were one man's act.
The copies survive. I will freely keep what we have recovered. I cannot swear for the people who refused.
One willing keeper of an account is enough to begin. Others may share that work. None may be given it by force.
Make the account public and I will leave its judgment with you. Release me quietly and preserve the record without opening every private memory.
Or carry the unresolved binding yourself. Or destroy me and lose what no copy holds.
Releasing you does not erase the house's crime. Protecting a family does not protect Edric from the record.
Then choose whose work begins when mine ends.
The ledger counts ash as fertilizer. The wagon totals match the refugee register.
Closing the mill stops the tainted channels. It also stops the flour coming through them.
The record leaves with us whatever we do to the machinery.
Good. Now decide how we feed the people who did not choose what was ground here.
Put the sword down far enough that my men can see what surrender looks like.
I was on that road in the war. Young enough to call an order the whole explanation.
Halvern refused to close the retreat. They hanged him. I closed it after him.
Now you take grain from travelers and call it repayment.
I said their houses owed ours. It became an excuse before I stopped needing it.
You can give testimony. You still answer for the people hurt this week.
My men have the custody terms. No levy can take their children for what I ordered.
I will speak. I am not asking the account to wipe the road clean.
Then sign the part you know. Leave the rest for the people who lived it.
The camp is packing. The signed account stays with you.
My men leave their blades for the grain they took.
Leaving does not make the missing travelers someone else's problem.
Sanctuary under the Vargan seal. Those were the words. They came because of the words.
What happened after you refused?
Rope. The yard. Dawn. Do not close it.
You cannot tell me about Edric. Your memory ends here.
I was ordered to retreat from another road. There were people we had promised to escort. I went.
I wrote that we could not hold. I left out that I never went back.
There are still people on the road.
The wax will not hold. They agreed to eat, Edric. They did not agree to carry the road.
I left civilians on a road after promising escort. I called it a retreat in my report. That part of my report was a lie.
Then do not ask us to sign yours because you finally stayed.
I will not. The copies establish what happened. Each of you decides whether to offer more.
Break the grain condition before you touch the seal. Otherwise the rite only learns a new way to threaten us.
Every household receives its allotment. No signature. My account comes afterward.
I left people behind under a retreat order. I stayed away and called it duty. That is my account before I ask for yours.
Then give people time to decide. A hand raised in relief is not an oath.
Some choose it now. Others choose the clean roots. I still treat them.
The cure was real. So was the choice I kept from them.
There will be shortages. I will not hide them behind a clean label.
I can tell you where the road ran. I have removed the family homes from the copy.
My grandmother kept these names. She did not leave me permission to hand you every private part of her life.
The road is evidence. The addresses are not.
You have the route. You do not have my promise to stand in a rite.
A record is not a person agreeing. Keep that straight.
I resealed the book after the novice died. Every year afterward I called it care.
I was afraid. That explains what I did. It does not give the unnamed people back their years.
My confession is my own. No household has to follow it to receive grain.
I found the command ledger six years ago. I sealed it. I was afraid of what the houses here would become without Vargan protection.
You inherited the crime. Keeping its proof hidden was your choice.
Yes. The renewal is my choice too. I need households to witness the seal before the grain moves.
People who must sign to feed their children cannot give you a free oath.
Then give me another way to get those carts through. Do not give me a principle and leave before winter.
I will testify without my seal. I will supply the road under the assembly's account.
Your title?
Not mine to shelter behind after this.
Your ledger is evidence. Your threatened words are not a new covenant.
At least we agree on the shape of what you are doing.
These pages establish what we recovered. They do not promise for the people who could not come.
Leave room for what the Hart knows that our copies do not.
People to return to. Not just work to finish.
I used to say the shrine kept the dead quiet. It kept their names apart.
What does each way cost?
Clean the rite and the danger moves out toward the wood. Open it and memory enters this place. Hold it shut and the next repair may tear it again.
None of those asks the dead what they wanted. A living witness can freely take the work of keeping their account. Not the right to make them disappear.
Oren said the name. Something opened. This is not him returned to answer us.
If we break it?
This vessel stops. Its memory disperses. If we keep it, we must stop treating every reaction as an invitation.
Or return the fragment where his name can hold it.
Yes. I can refine the oil whichever way you choose. I will not price a formula against a child's memory.
The creatures gathered what the road could no longer hide. The wire came later.
Vargan tried to contain the evidence.
Keep that fact. This fragment cannot tell us everything that happened.
Oren was making something someone had erased readable again.
Keeping this close gives me time. It also leaves everyone else waiting for an account.
What matters is whether I returned after asking them to change.
The people who died can be named. Where their grandchildren sleep is not the same fact.
Bram found the tokens in the repaired road. Sella brought one for a burial reading. Oren restored the first name beneath his paint.
The name loosened what the hidden road had kept disordered.
And my thread failed to contain it. Vargan's men came afterward for the tokens.
Now Edric wants those households at a renewal. No signature, no grain. Your copies will reach them before his guards do.
I carry an account from Greyfen's road.
Then you had better let me show it.
Why are household signatures beside grain allotments?
Terms offered to someone hungry do not make a free promise.
Did your orders include scratching out their names?
You kept both?
Your soldiers reclaimed the tokens after the road repairs.
I ordered containment. The repairs had exposed a cache the shrine could no longer quiet.
You also kept the ledger closed for six years.
Yes. Before you ask the next question, know that I have no smaller word for that.
The command survived without the names. The register has the names without the command.
Together they establish who did what. Copy the page before any choice about its seal.
The wheel has sunk to its hub. Rook braces the cart while the driver tries not to fall against it.
If you are hunting something expensive, consider this wheel. It has eaten my entire morning.
Move your hand from the spoke. I will take the weight.
Then Anwen gets the driver, and the sacks get through the gate. In that order.
The cart stands on dry boards. The driver has Anwen's cup between both hands.
Grain inside. Person inside. A profitable morning by standards I have apparently lowered.
Put the clean boards over the rut. Leave the marked pieces where we can read them.
Repair the route without burying what it exposed.
People can pass here. The evidence has not gone back under their wheels.
An order can move grain. It cannot make a hungry person's oath free.
You may put your hand to one of those without agreeing to stand before the Hart.
Then keep the names of helpers away from the renewal seal.
Practical help before an oath. Nobody has to become evidence to receive it.
A short ration is a cost. So is using tainted machinery. The ledger does not make either disappear.
Keep the record whatever method gets the flour through.
Clean repair takes time. For now, these sacks are what keeps the closure from becoming another barred gate.
It gets flour through today. It does not settle what went into the channels or the work of replacing them.
The accounts stay public. Repair is work that people can return to see.
Copies prove the crime. A new promise must belong to the person who makes it. No ration list can lend somebody else's consent.
Anwen puts three empty cups beside the coat Oren left. Rook waits by the door.
The creatures gathered their belongings. Someone alive bound the token afterward and tried to remove it.
I recognize the old carving. You can give it to me, show the village, or keep it while we make copies.
If you show it, show the people behind it a way to stay safe as well.
I will stay. The payment ends the hunt. It does not settle what I now know.
A moment, hunter. The man behind that screen cannot reach his water.
The cup is on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.
And that little coat on the bench belongs under the shelf. Oren will complain if I let the rain into his pockets.
Thank you for the water. He has stopped trying to stand.
Would you move that little coat under the shelf? Oren left it here this morning. He said he would be too hot.
You found a dry place for his coat. Thank you.
The man behind the screen needs the cup on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.
There. Close enough that he need not ask again.
Was he with the missing cart?
No. A fall on the south road. Not every hurt here is a sign, Kael. Some people only need water.
That is Oren's. Leave the pockets turned in; he keeps things in them.
Did you mend this?
He did. I threaded the needle. He would not let me do the rest.
Bram drove the cart. Sella took Oren beside her. He left this because the sun was out.
I cannot promise nobody will ask what you took. I can promise supper is not a reward for obeying him.
Then you speak for yourselves. Lowering a weapon does not sign your name to anyone else's account.
Mind the corner. That sack has already had a worse journey than either of us.
The wheel will need lifting before it can turn.
It will. The flour needed feeding to people before it needed feeding to mud.
A woman at the kitchen opens the sack and measures three small shares. She keeps the string for mending.
There. Something went where we said it would. I could get used to that.
The kitchen has the flour. The cart is lighter.
I've told them you did the heavy bit. Don't make me a liar by offering to do it all again.
Leave the peg proud. Someone will need to pull it out when the next flood comes.
You expect it to fail?
I expect someone to repair it. A thing can be well made without being the last thing anyone ever makes.
Water threads through the cleared drain. Rook's empty wheel crosses the boards without sinking.
There. A road ought to carry the person using it. Start with that.
Water's still moving. Boards are still holding.
If you're looking for praise, ask the wheel. It made the most noise about it before.
Did anyone ask what they had to promise?
One woman did.
And?
I told her the basket was not a contract.
Tell her again tomorrow. People don't learn that sort of thing in one meal.
I thought writing them where everyone could see would make my hands stop shaking.
It made you begin.
Bram. Sella. Oren. I have practiced saying the names of the dead more often than I have spoken to the people who miss them.
A man waiting at the wall asks who will pay for the land his mother was refused. Anwen puts his question beneath the names instead of sending him away.
We cannot promise every answer today.
We can promise this question will still be here tomorrow.
Anwen leaves room on the board. The public account is no longer a ceremony that ends when the bell stops.
Tor has begun measuring timber. Rook is arguing about who gets the first load. Go help them make this more than my handwriting.
This copy names the offices, the orders and those who gave them. This other book belongs to the families.
Who can open it?
The people whose lives it holds. They may let someone else read. They may refuse.
A woman returns a sealed page. She asks Anwen to keep her son's name and destroy the account of his last fear. Anwen asks once whether she is certain, then follows her instruction.
Edric's order stays on the wall.
Yes. His privacy was never the thing we were protecting.
For the first time, the bell can mourn someone without claiming everything that happened to them.
The living still need timber and flour. Tor is at the bench. There is a world outside these books.
The silence held through the night. I kept waking to make sure.
I felt the road when I woke. Not words. Weight.
Then we write the limits now, while people are grateful enough to forget them. You did not accept every order anyone might give you.
She writes that the keeping is Kael's choice. No child inherits it. No shortage can compel another keeper. The old command remains beside it, uncensored.
If I cannot keep it?
We meet again. We tell the truth about the cost. We do not turn your promise into an excuse to stop thinking.
Kael reads the lines before signing. The tremor in his hand is his own.
Tor has a repair for you. Something ordinary. Let him do it.
Nothing answered when I rang the bell.
Were you hoping it would?
I don't know. That is the honest answer today.
The copied command and the household register lie on her table. Human hands saved them before the glade burned. Their evidence has not become less true because its witness is gone.
There are things we can no longer ask. We must mark those gaps instead of filling them with convenient answers.
A father passing the table says his child slept without hearing voices. Anwen listens until he has finished.
We keep what remains. And answer for what we chose.
Tor needs another pair of hands. The next repair cannot wait for us to feel certain.
The west field wants its gate. The kitchen wants its cart. The chapel wants a board large enough to accuse the whole county.
The chapel can have the offcuts.
Who decides whose repair comes first?
Today? The people standing here. Tomorrow we'll need something better than whoever shouts loudest.
Put that on Anwen's board.
Where does that go?
To someone who asked me not to tell everyone where it goes.
You can still count the flour without counting the family's grief.
Keeping a confidence used to mean hiding my own part. I'll have to learn the difference.
Ask whose safety the silence serves.
Sit. If you're going to stand watch, you can at least stop this buckle cutting your shoulder.
There are other repairs.
This is one of them.
Help isn't the same thing as taking your oath. We can carry supper without carrying the Hart.
Come back before it splits again. That is a request, not a sacred duty.
It got everywhere. Doesn't mean everything is ruined.
No. Doesn't mean it didn't cost anything either.
I cannot put it back.
I didn't ask you to. Hold this end.
Listen. I missed that. We can miss what was lost and still be glad to hear it.
A public promise has a place people can return to.
Will you be here when they arrive?
I said I would keep it.
They asked for a marker. Nothing more.
Then it can be nothing more.
How far does it follow you?
I will have to learn.
Then don't answer for all the years today.
Will it grow?
We can water it. We can come back.
You still have Oren's coat.
The cuff is stiff with mud. I keep folding that part underneath.
What happens if you wash it?
Then it's a clean coat. I know that, but I keep behaving as if I'll have sent him away a second time.
You kept the empty baskets?
For the next meals. One handle's nearly through, and the woman who carried it apologized to me.
For the handle?
For needing the basket. I started explaining why she needn't, then I fetched some twine.
You've rewritten the labels.
The first ones were tidy and small. Especially the word ash.
Too small to read?
No, small enough for me to hope they wouldn't. These are less tidy.
New labels?
For the clean roots. I found room to write every steeping time.
And the other jar?
Still the old label. I keep finding very necessary work on the other side of the table.
You reached for that empty space.
The old jar stood there for years. My hand gets ahead of me.
What brings it back?
The kettle; the clean roots need longer, so I watch them. Waiting turns out to be part of treating someone.
Bram charged you for only one axle.
The second repair was free if I held the wheel and stopped advising him.
Did you manage both?
The wheel stayed up. He took what victories he could.
Can I still ask about the road?
You can ask. If I say a place stays off the page, it stays off.
Even when the route passes it?
Especially then. A road goes past a great many doors it hasn't been invited through.
Here, where I can see who's coming.
You used to answer with a joke.
I still have them. I'm saving the good ones for a room that doesn't feel like an address you've handed out.
Ask where it goes. Don't ask me to draw the houses back in.
You remember them all?
The doors, mostly, and which ones opened. A blank sheet doesn't make that a blank part of my life.
What did you use to grind the marks away?
That stone. Still cuts.
Why keep it beside the named work?
So I have to reach past it. I said 'still useful' about the iron, too, and I don't want the words coming out before I've thought.
You still use it?
On an edge, not on a name. I can remember the difference without pretending I need a different stone.
That stone. It wasn't in the bundle I handed over.
Forgotten?
No, the families decide what happens to their iron. This bit is mine to remember.
What was wrong with my grip?
You held the hammer as if the board might answer back.
I've worked with worse company.
Board's better company if you loosen your thumb. Head does the striking.
You keep turning the seal in your hand.
I used to do that while someone gave me a number. It made an answer wait until I was ready for it.
Does it help now?
No, I'm discovering how long a silence can be when nobody has to fill it for me.
You still have the seal.
You have the ledger. Must I empty my pockets for this conversation?
I asked about the seal.
It used to mean people waited for my answer. Now they watch for what I'll try to keep.
You've rubbed the edge of the seal smooth.
It was smooth before you arrived.
I didn't notice.
You were occupied with getting an answer out of me. This one, at least, I can give without your help.
You read their refusal?
Twice. First I looked for a sentence someone must have put in their mouths.
And the second?
I recognized the way they complain. I used to interrupt before they reached the point.
The copy with the homes left out. I noticed the gaps before I listened to the words.
Did the gaps change what they said?
No, they just left me fewer places to look instead.
The sanctuary order is copied. You don't have to give it again.
Sanctuary under the Vargan seal.
I have that line.
Do not close it. There are still people on the road.
I hear you.
